It is the earlier letter transmitting the temporary unemployment-compensation legislation expressly recalled by the child, while the child presents permanent improvements to the same Federal-State system. Both letters move through the same sequence: transmit legislation, invoke the February 2 unemployment program, describe unemployment statistics and exhausted benefits, explain relief to workers and families through restored purchasing power, connect that relief to economic recovery or stability, and identify enclosed explanatory material from the Secretary of Labor. C13 and C02 share the Labor Department, unemployment or employment context, and similar transmittal-letter structure, but neither matches the child's specific unemployment-compensation machinery as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"You will recall that in my message to the Congress of February 2nd, which recommended a program of temporary extended unemployment compensation, I pointed out the need for permanent improvements in the system.","parent_excerpt":"I am transmitting herewith two bills: (1) To establish a temporary program for the payment of additional unemployment compensation to workers who have exhausted their State benefits... I recommended such legislation on February 2","explanation":"The child explicitly presents its permanent program as the successor to the temporary unemployment-compensation initiative transmitted in C16."},{"child_excerpt":"there are still 4.8 million Americans out of work and 900,000 of them have been unemployed for more than six months.","parent_excerpt":"In January, 5.4 million workers were without jobs... about one-half million who had already exhausted their unemployment compensation were still unemployed.","explanation":"Both letters justify legislation with closely parallel unemployment statistics emphasizing prolonged unemployment or exhausted benefits."},{"child_excerpt":"Enactment of the draft bill will to some extent alleviate the suffering of unemployed workers and their families, and will help stabilize the economy by increasing the purchasing power of such workers.","parent_excerpt":"Unemployment compensation provides unemployed workers with necessary purchasing power... This has a serious impact not only on the worker and his family, but on the economic health of the entire economy.","explanation":"This is a distinctive shared policy rationale linking unemployment benefits, workers and families, purchasing power, and the health of the wider economy."},{"child_excerpt":"Also enclosed is a letter from the Secretary of Labor together with an explanatory statement describing the draft legislation in detail.","parent_excerpt":"The enclosed letters from the Secretary of Labor and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare describe the legislation in more detail.","explanation":"The child retains the same administrative enclosure mechanism, narrowed to the Secretary of Labor and an explanatory statement."}]}
